Export mgcv neighbourhood structures

Source: R/nei.R
as_nei.Rd

The result is a plain list of one-based indices, with cumulative endpoints. No rescaling of repeated assessments or covariance settings is performed. Neighbourhood sampling preserves the complete structure needed by bam. Export requires at least two folds for compatibility with the tested mgcv integration. Single native folds remain usable for inspection and rsample. In mgcv 1.9-4, scalar sampling incorrectly samples packed endpoints for nonsingleton omissions. For these designs, supply at least two explicit fold numbers, or omit sample to use every fold. This compatibility restriction is enforced without requiring mgcv to be installed.

Usage

as_nei(
  x,
  sample = NULL,
  jackknife = NULL,
  max_bytes = getOption("naboer.max_bytes", 1024^3),
  data = NULL
)

Arguments

x

A naboer_folds object.

sample

Optional bam sampling specification: one positive count, or a vector of neighbourhood numbers. A length-one value always means a count and is supported only when every omission set is a singleton.

jackknife

Optional logical gam covariance setting. NULL preserves mgcv's default by omitting the field.

max_bytes

Maximum estimated packed output size in bytes; defaults to option naboer.max_bytes, or 1 GiB. Use Inf to disable the memory guard.

data

Optional data used for alignment checking. Supply unchanged canonical data, or data containing the original unique identifier column.

Value

A plain list with a, ma, d, md, and optional settings.
